A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZPressor and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, efficiency measurements, ablations, ACID generalization results, and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated anchor-selection alternatives, confidence-based pruning comparisons, and an IB-loss ablation.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an explicit KL-regularized training objective in Eq. (8), evaluates a nonzero regularization weight, and describes alternative anchor-selection procedures. The default FPS selection and attention architecture remain unchanged. Section 4.1 still denies additional regularization, leaving its use in the main experiments unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate novel-view synthesis on DL3DV and RE10K, transfer to ACID, and extremely dense inputs. The new 'pose-free' row changes anchor selection within the existing DL3DV evaluation; it does not establish a separate fully unposed reconstruction task or new data coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix Table C adds MVSplat with confidence-based pruning at two pruning ratios as a comparator to ZPressor. Table B also compares alternative anchor selectors. Existing DepthSplat, MVSplat, and pixelSplat benchmark comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols compare selectors with 36 DL3DV views, test pruning with 24 RE10K views at ratios 0.75 and 0.5, and compare IB weights 0 and 10^-5. Table C explicitly states retraining and matches Gaussian counts at ratio 0.75. Original split, resolution, budget, and metric descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2-A.4 substantially extend the design analysis: they test FPS against overlap and clustering alternatives, compression against confidence pruning, and architectural benefits separately from IB regularization. These address previously untested design questions while retaining the original fusion, attention, bottleneck, generalization, and failure analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, specific seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's statement that K-means is deterministic given a seed does not document an experimental seed or an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and A retain their values, but Tables B-D add substantive findings on selection, pruning, and regularization. Table B reports 23.88 dB for FPS versus 21.49, 22.81, and 22.84 for alternative selectors. Table C reports 21.15/26.94 dB for pruning ratios 0.75/0.5 versus 27.49 for ZPressor. Table D reports 23.43 versus 23.88 dB for IB weights 0 and 10^-5. These are additional comparisons, not across-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Eq. (8) adds a probabilistic objective combining expected negative log-likelihood with a weighted posterior-to-prior KL term, including a Gaussian prior definition. v1 provides the mutual-information formulation and rendering-loss discussion without this explicit objective. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated bottleneck from encoder capacity to the capacity of the whole image-to-3DGS network, attributing overload to excessive feature tokens. The central compression, scalability, and benchmark-performance contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of Figure 6 to discuss ambiguity and noisier representations from redundant anchors. New appendix interpretations distinguish pruning's loss of spatial coverage from compression and describe IB loss as an auxiliary regularizer. The extreme-density limitations and societal-impact discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents overlap computation, feature-space and camera-position clustering, pruning ratios and retraining, and tested IB coefficients. Existing architecture details, learning rates, hardware, training duration, and code/model access statements remain unchanged. The posterior construction and conflicting regularization descriptions still leave implementation ambiguity.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bai et al.'s information-bottleneck work on robot manipulation to the related-work discussion. Other reference changes chiefly update bibliographic metadata or numbering; the paper's overall positioning relative to prior reconstruction and compression methods remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 adds numbered related-work and appendix subsections, expands the bottleneck explanation, revises terminology, and updates affiliation, conference, and acknowledgement text. The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds appendix Tables B-D, enlarges the main benchmark tables, and relocates algorithms and appendix figures, including grouping Figures C-E on one page. Existing figure imagery and plotted findings are retained; the changes are localized rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new anchor-selection and matched-Gaussian-count pruning controls provide better support for design choices than v1, while preserving the original benchmark evidence. The benefit is limited by the conflict between Eq. (8)/Table D and Section 4.1's assertion of no additional regularization, which leaves the training recipe and attribution of unchanged headline scores unclear.
